correctness.rationale: Exact expectation follows from per-column event probability p^t-p^m. The critical threshold proof uses union and exponential bounds uniform across 2^m subsets, an O(m^-1/4) binomial band, summable Markov–Borel–Cantelli errors, and the central limit theorem. The two zero-one sides follow from exponential summable expectations. The large-deviation exponent is sandwiched between binomial tails of slopes c/(-log p)±epsilon or by the deterministic top-subset lower bound. A separate exhaustive matrix enumerator verifies all 29 finite parameter cases but does not prove the infinite statements.

value.rationale: Intensional stability is an established and widely used FCA robustness invariant. For the natural top concept of a Bernoulli null-model context, exponential attribute growth yields a previously uncharacterized intrinsic threshold: an exact annealed expectation, an almost-sure Gaussian crossover (not just a mean law), and a precise exponential decay rate. This addresses calibration and sensitivity of actual concept stability under high-dimensional incidence noise. The object is canonical, parameters are structural rather than arbitrary slices, and the result does not rely on a downstream conjecture.
